records.rationale: The driver limits frame count but not bytes before copying into a kernel USB transmit buffer. Bounding each record and maintaining the running length repair device-transfer construction, not a shared userspace packet library.

records.affected_operation: Bounding accumulated fragment lengths before tailroom allocation
records.rationale: A narrowed kernel accumulator wraps and under-allocates skb tailroom; the internal drop-reason header supports rejection rather than exporting the vulnerable operation.

records.affected_operation: Rejecting playback packet sizes that exceed the allocated URB slice
records.rationale: Endpoint metadata influences a kernel audio-driver buffer write before USB submission. The involved memcpy/memset and URB lifetime are runtime kernel behavior rather than userspace audio-library code.

records.component: ALSA caiaq USB device probe cleanup
records.affected_operation: Failing probe after an input device was already registered
records.rationale: Registered input-device strings point into freed kernel sound-device state after probe failure. Reading a uevent attribute exposes that stale reference, but the implementation needing repair is kernel registration teardown.

records.affected_operation: Rechecking shutdown before using an association after sleep
records.rationale: Kernel wait processing releases the socket lock and may drop the final association reference; sendmsg/shutdown calls trigger the race, not userspace implementation.

records.affected_operation: Removing published rules and waiting for readers before dropping executable marks
records.rationale: The freed fsnotify mark remains visible through kernel audit RCU lists. Administrative rule installation and watched-directory changes are triggers, not implementation in userspace audit tools.

records.affected_operation: Retrying nested guest entry after acquiring nested pages failed
records.rationale: A userspace VMM can retry KVM_RUN, but KVM retains stale unpinned page-frame mappings if the acquisition request is not re-pended. This is kernel nested-MMU state management, not userspace header behavior.
